_source: ADR Chapter 3.3 — special provisions. PART 5 — numbers 651–674.

provisions.651: Provision V2(1) need not be applied if the net mass of explosive substances per transport unit is ≤4000 kg, provided the net mass per vehicle is ≤3000 kg.
provisions.652: Receptacles of austenitic or duplex stainless steel, or welded titanium, that do not meet the requirements of Chapter 6.2 but are approved under national aviation regulations (fuel for hot-air balloons/aircraft put into service before 1 July 2004) may be carried by road under detailed conditions: aviation design approval, a reduced calculation pressure (at +40°C), permitted materials (titanium Rm>450 MPa, duplex steel up to 85% Re), pressure-relief devices (26 bar nominal / 30 bar test), external insulation ≥25 mm, protection in a cage, marking restricting use to hot-air balloons/aircraft, and a service life ≤25 years.
provisions.654: Waste lighters collected separately and consigned per 5.4.1.1.3 may be carried for disposal without protection against accidental release, provided pressure build-up is prevented; packed per P003 with additional requirements (rigid packagings ≤60 l, filled with water or protective material, ignition devices covered, ventilation, carriage in ventilated or open vehicles); leaking/deformed lighters must go in salvage packagings; special provision 201 and packing instruction provisions PP84/RR5 (P002) do not apply.
provisions.655: Cylinders for breathing apparatus that comply with the PED Directive (97/23/EC or 2014/68/EU) but do not meet Chapter 6.2 may be carried provided they are tested per 6.2.1.6.1 and the periodic inspection interval of P200 is observed; the hydraulic test pressure is the pressure marked under the PED Directive.
provisions.657: Entry applies only to technically pure substances; for LPG mixture components see UN 1965 or UN 1075 with NOTE 2 in 2.2.2.3.
provisions.658: UN 1057 LIGHTERS (complying with EN ISO 9994:2019) and LIGHTER REFILLS — only selected provisions of 3.4 apply (without the 30 kg/20 kg mass limits), provided: gross mass per package ≤10 kg, total mass per vehicle/container ≤100 kg, and the outer packaging is durably marked.
provisions.659: Materials requiring removal of air from the vapour space (packing provisions PP86/TP7) may not be carried under this generic entry — they must be carried under their own UN number.
provisions.662: Cylinders that do not meet Chapter 6.2, used exclusively on board a ship or aircraft, may be carried for filling/testing and return, provided they comply with a recognized standard, valves are protected (4.1.6.8), marking is per 5.2.1/5.2.2, and filling meets the requirements of P200; the transport document must state "Carriage in accordance with special provision 662".
provisions.663-664: Entry for empty, uncleaned packagings/IBCs/large packagings (waste) that held goods of Classes 3, 4.1, 5.1, 6.1, 8, 9 and are destined for disposal or recycling (not reconditioning/repair/reuse), containing only adhering residues; excluded: PG I, entries marked "0" in column 7a, desensitized explosives, self-reactive substances, radioactive material, asbestos, PCBs. General rules: Class 5.1 residues must not be co-loaded with residues of other classes; documented sorting procedures at the point of loading are required. Separately: tanks carrying this material may be fitted with additive dispensers (for UN 1202/1993 PG III or UN 3082, or dangerous goods) — with detailed construction requirements (wall thickness per material), approvals, capacity limits (400 l for the permanently fitted variant), testing, and a transport document entry ("additive dispenser"); no additional driver training is required; the tank's large placards do not apply to the dispenser.
provisions.665: Unground hard coal, coke, and anthracite meeting the Class 4.2, PG III criteria — not subject to ADR.
provisions.666: Vehicles/equipment powered by a battery (special provision 388), carried as cargo together with the dangerous goods needed for their operation, are not subject to the other provisions of ADR provided: liquid fuel valves are closed (vehicle upright), the valve is closed and the circuit broken for gaseous fuel, and metal hydride storage systems are approved by the competent authority; does not apply to vehicles emptied of fuel (definitions given in the notes); fully enclosed, unidentifiable vehicles must be marked per Chapter 5.2; the alternative for sodium ion batteries is special provision 404.
provisions.667: Lithium or sodium ion cells and batteries in damaged or defective vehicles, engines, or machinery are exempted from 2.2.9.1.7.1/.2 provided: (i) where the damage does not affect safety → carried under special provision 363 or 666; (ii) where the damage affects safety → the cell/battery is removed and carried under special provision 376 (or, where removal would be unsafe or is not possible, the vehicle is towed away or carried under (i)); the same procedures apply to damaged/defective cells or batteries removed from such vehicles.
provisions.668: Road-surfacing material and bituminous material for surface repair, carried at elevated temperature, are not subject to the other requirements of ADR if: they do not meet the criteria of any class other than Class 9, the boiler surface temperature is ≤70°C, the boiler is tightly closed, and the boiler capacity is ≤3000 l.
provisions.669: Trailers fitted with equipment powered by liquid, gaseous or electric fuel for use during carriage are classified as UN 3166/3171/3556/3557/3558, carried as cargo under the conditions of those entries, with total liquid fuel tank capacity ≤500 l.
provisions.670-671: Lithium or sodium ion cells and batteries in household appliances (e.g. refrigerator/washing machine controllers) collected for treatment, dismantling, recycling or disposal are exempted from ADR (including from special provision 376) when they are not the main power source, the appliance contains no other main lithium/sodium ion cells or batteries, and they are adequately protected. Those not meeting these conditions (destined for intermediate processing) are exempted subject to: packing per P909 or strong outer packagings specially designed (with suitable protection against damage/loss of contents), a quality assurance programme (limit of 333 kg per transport unit), and marking "LITHIUM/SODIUM ION BATTERIES FOR DISPOSAL/RECYCLING" (on the packaging or on the vehicle when carried in bulk or on pallets). For the 1.1.3.6 exemption: transport category follows the packing group of the consignment (PG I → category 1, PG II → category 2, PG III → category 3; no packing group → category 2).
provisions.672: Articles (machines, apparatus, devices) complying with special provision 301 are not subject to the other provisions of ADR when packed in a strong outer packaging per 4.1.1.1, or carried without outer packaging where they otherwise provide adequate protection on their own.
provisions.674: Applies to the periodic inspection and testing of over-moulded cylinders (definition in 1.2.1) — permits alternative methods to 6.2.1.6.1(d) (destructive testing in place of the standard test), based on: basic manufacturing series/production subgroups, traceability (marking plus electronic identification plus a central database), random sampling for statistical evaluation, burst/adhesion/blister-rust tests per EN 1442/EN 14140/EN ISO 4628-3, and detailed statistical methodology (SPC sample-result charts, tolerance factors k3 for normal and Weibull distributions) — the full numerical tables and formulas are omitted here as too detailed for this reference; for over-moulded cylinders it is sufficient to note that special provision 674 exists, with reference to the full ADR text for the details.
